blockers: CORE_CAUSAL_MODEL_DISTORTED remains open: replacing household backup-water capacity with naturally lower baseline demand removes the previous contradiction but does not establish a valid reason to assign households the deepest restriction. Lower demand can make a restriction save less water, while the cited household-only restriction examples do not establish this proposed rule. The residential-air-conditioning explanation is also ungrounded because ordinary household AC is not a material municipal-water demand mechanism.

The current fact sheet still defines sector allocation using alternative means and explicitly includes household groundwater/desalination, contradicting the adopted capacity-based scoring model and leaving the authoritative design chain causally inconsistent.
medium: c_compression_v3.json correctly lists rate of reservoir decline under removed_complexity, but reason_for_removal then says that rate was integrated into current reservoir level and rain timing. Those snapshots do not encode a rate, so the disclosure still implies representation after declaring the variable removed.

reference_research_v3.json repeatedly describes the adopted sector mechanic as timing circumstances × alternative means and says every sector, including households, becomes correct when those conditions align. This is stale relative to the adopted household baseline-demand rule.
low: The adopted t5 goal begins with a change log from t1 and several fields repeatedly cite prior review fixes. Its operative interaction is understandable on its own, but removing diff-oriented language would make it a cleaner implementation specification.

failure_codes.finding: Household baseline demand being naturally lower is not a grounded proxy for capacity to bear the deepest cut. It may reduce the water saved by cutting that sector, and neither the cited household-only restriction observations nor the cooler-week/AC assertion establishes the scoring rule.

The current fact sheet continues to specify alternative means—including household groundwater and desalination—as decision-critical allocation information, contradicting the adopted model's claimed separation of those resources from household scoring.
The compression artifact says decline rate was removed but also says it was integrated into two snapshot axes that do not represent rate.
The reference artifact still defines the sector mechanic through alternative means and applies that characterization to households, conflicting with t5 and design-sim v3.
